name: Helfer
description: Small offline pocket tools for fire brigades (Feuerwehr) in one Android app, built with .NET and Avalonia. Each helper can get its own launcher icon; the first one is a Stoppuhr (stopwatch) for exercises. No network permission, no account, no telemetry. "Helfer" is a working name.
description_good_justification: The README opens with what the app is, who it is for and which helpers it has, in German for the fire-brigade audience, with an English developer section below: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/blob/main/README.md
interact_justification: GitHub Discussions with four German categories (Ankündigungen, Fragen & Antworten, Ideen, Aus der Praxis): https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/discussions. The issue chooser routes questions and ideas there and bugs and features to issue forms: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/tree/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md, linked from the README, covers the first contribution, development setup, workflow, commit conventions and how to add a helper: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires Conventional Commits, DCO sign-off, signed commits, green CI, a changelog entry for src/ changes and screenshots for UI changes; branch protection enforces signatures, DCO and the CI checks: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
documentation_basics_justification: The README covers each helper, the per-helper launcher icons, installation from GitHub releases and how to verify a download: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/blob/main/README.md. Building, testing and releasing are in the developer section and https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/blob/main/docs/releasing.md
documentation_interface_justification: The only external interface is the Android user interface, described helper by helper in the README. The app has no network interface, no file format and no API, so there is nothing else to document.
sites_https_justification: The project site is the GitHub repository, served over HTTPS: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer
english_justification: Developer documentation, issues, pull requests, commit messages and code comments are English. The user interface is German by design, because the users are German fire brigades.
maintained_justification: The repository was started in November 2026 and is under active development; every change lands through a reviewed pull request: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/commits/main
repo_track_justification: git, so every change has an author, a timestamp and a parent.
repo_interim_justification: Every change reaches main through a pull request, so interim work is public on branches and in the PR before it is released: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/pulls?q=is%3Apr
version_unique_justification: Releases are cut from vX.Y.Z tags by https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml, which builds the release and derives the Android versionCode from the tag. No release has been tagged yet.
version_semver_justification: Semantic Versioning, with tags of the form vX.Y.Z and pre-releases as vX.Y.Z-rc.N. The project is pre-1.0, so breaking changes may occur in any release until then.
version_tags_justification: Releases will be tagged vX.Y.Z; see https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/blob/main/docs/releasing.md. No tag exists yet.
release_notes_justification: CHANGELOG.md follows Keep a Changelog and is assembled with towncrier from one fragment per pull request, which CI requires; the GitHub release carries those notes. No release has been cut yet: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No vulnerability has been reported or fixed in the project to date, so no release note has had to identify one. The changelog has a Security section for when that changes.
report_process_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to report a bug, and the issue forms ask for the version, the phone and Android version, the steps and the expected versus actual behaviour: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/tree/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE
report_responses_justification: No bug report has been filed yet. Reports are answered in the issue: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/issues?q=is%3Aissue
enhancement_responses_justification: No enhancement request has been filed yet. Ideas are discussed under Ideen before they become an issue: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/discussions/categories/ideen
report_archive_justification: GitHub Issues and Discussions are publicly readable and permanently archived: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/issues
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md documents the process and is linked from the README, CONTRIBUTING.md and the issue chooser: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled on the Security tab. SECURITY.md gives the steps and states that vulnerabilities must not go in public issues, discussions or pull requests: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability has been reported in the last six months, which is the case the criterion says to answer N/A for.
build_justification: dotnet build, wrapped by a Makefile, with the SDK version pinned in global.json; the Android package is built in a digest-pinned Docker image: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/blob/main/Makefile
build_common_tools_justification: The .NET SDK and MSBuild, both widely used and freely available.
build_floss_tools_justification: The .NET SDK is MIT-licensed FLOSS and the build and tests run on Linux in CI. The Android package additionally needs the Android SDK; a Docker-based build is provided so it can be built without installing anything locally.
test_justification: About 60 test methods across four xUnit projects, including a headless Avalonia render suite that exercises the real views at phone size: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/tree/main/tests
test_invocation_justification: dotnet test, or make test, optionally narrowed with PROJECT= and FILTER=.
test_most_justification: Measured by mutation testing (Stryker.NET), which checks that the tests notice a change, not only that they run a line. A pull request that changes .cs files in Core, AppLogic or a helper (today Helpers.Stoppuhr) fails below 80% on the lines it changed. A weekly run mutates each of those projects whole and fails below the floor of 72 set in its stryker-config.json. The views in Helfer.Ui are not mutated; they are covered by the headless render tests instead: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/blob/main/.github/workflows/mutation.yml
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions builds and tests every push and pull request: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENTS.md require tests with new functionality, a failing test first for a bug fix, and the pull-request template carries the checklist: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
tests_are_added_justification: The scaffold and every helper ship with tests, and the README screenshots are produced by a test, so they cannot drift from the app: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/tree/main/tests
tests_documented_added_justification: The policy is written down in CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENTS.md: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/blob/main/AGENTS.md
warnings_justification: Directory.Build.props sets AnalysisMode=All and AnalysisLevel=10.0, enables nullable reference types and adds StyleCop.Analyzers to every project. CI additionally runs dotnet format whitespace and style with --verify-no-changes.
warnings_fixed_justification: TreatWarningsAsErrors=true, so any warning fails the build and therefore the pull request; Avalonia's XAML deprecations are escalated separately. There is no backlog of tolerated warnings. The rules that are switched off are switched off in .editorconfig, each with its reason beside it: CA2007 and CA1716 app-wide, the StyleCop documentation and ordering rules, a few noise rules in test code, and CA1308, CA2000 and CA2213 in the Android head, where the Android runtime owns object lifetimes. CS1591 is suppressed in Directory.Build.props: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/blob/main/.editorconfig
warnings_strict_justification: Warnings are errors, analysis mode is the strictest setting rather than the default subset, and the format checks are enforced in CI rather than advisory.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer has a long background in open-source infrastructure software and handles security advisories for it. Here that shows as an app that requests no Android permissions at all, least privilege in every CI workflow, actions pinned to commit SHAs and a zizmor audit of every workflow.
know_common_errors_justification: The attack surface is kept small on purpose: no network permission, no file import, no exported component beyond the launcher entries, and launcher intents are only matched against the app's own aliases. AGENTS.md records the rules for input that crosses a trust boundary should a helper ever add one: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/blob/main/AGENTS.md#security
crypto_published_justification: The software uses no cryptography: no network, no encryption and no signing at runtime. Release integrity relies on GitHub's HTTPS, SHA-256 checksums and Sigstore build provenance, not on code in this project.
crypto_call_justification: The software implements and calls no cryptography; src/ contains no use of System.Security.Cryptography.
crypto_keylength_justification: The software uses no cryptography, so it has no keys.
crypto_working_justification: The software uses no cryptographic algorithm.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: The software uses no cryptographic algorithm.
crypto_pfs_justification: The software does not communicate over a network: the app declares no INTERNET permission.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The software has no user accounts and no login, so it stores no passwords.
crypto_random_justification: The software generates no keys, nonces or other security-relevant random values.
delivery_mitm_justification: Releases are downloaded from GitHub over HTTPS, with build provenance attested through Sigstore: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/releases
delivery_unsigned_justification: Every download is over HTTPS, so no hash is ever retrieved over plain HTTP. The release's SHA256SUMS.txt is served over HTTPS from the same GitHub release, and the APK itself carries Sigstore build provenance that `gh attestation verify` checks independently of the checksum file.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No vulnerability has been reported, so nothing of medium or higher severity is unpatched. Dependabot alerts and security updates are enabled, and weekly version updates cover GitHub Actions, Docker, pip and NuGet.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: There are no known unpatched vulnerabilities of any severity.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No key, certificate or credential file is committed, and there are no hardcoded secrets in src/. The Play upload key stays on the maintainer's machine and is passed to the build as a file mount, never as an argument.
static_analysis_justification: Two independent tools. CodeQL with the security-and-quality suite runs on every pull request, every push to main and weekly, with results in the Code Scanning tab and a required check on main: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml. The .NET analyzers run at AnalysisMode=All with warnings as errors.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's security-and-quality suite is explicitly vulnerability-focused, and no CA3xxx injection or CA5xxx security analyzer rule is suppressed in the build.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Alerts are driven to zero rather than triaged into a backlog. A finding is fixed in code by default; a query is excluded only where it duplicates an analyzer rule the build already governs, with the reason written beside it: https://github.com/CodeForFire/helfer/blob/main/.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml
static_analysis_often_justification: On every pull request and every push to main, plus a weekly scheduled run so that newly released queries reach existing code even when the repository is quiet.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No fuzzing or runtime instrumentation today. The app reads no input the user did not type, so there is no parser to fuzz yet; this is revisited when a helper imports data.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: C# is memory-safe and the project contains no unsafe blocks and no native code of its own.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Debug builds enable assertions, and the test suite runs with them enabled.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis is run, so it has produced no findings to fix.
